approachQuestion.prompt:
Nested Signal Strings

Return all strings containing exactly p copies of "(" and p copies of ")" in which every prefix has at least as many opening as closing symbols. Each string must appear once, in any order.

Examples:
p=2 -> ["(())","()()"].
p=1 -> ["()"].

Constraints: 1 <= p <= 11. Output strings have length 2p.

options.text: Track opened and closed counts. Add an opening symbol only while openings remain, and a closing symbol only while closed<opened; emit at length 2p.
options.feedback: The inequalities are necessary for every valid prefix and leave every valid continuation reachable. Both budgets must be exhausted before emitting.

options.text: Allow either symbol until each total reaches p; accept every resulting string.
options.feedback: For p=1, this also accepts ")(", whose first prefix is invalid.

options.text: Whenever an opening symbol is appended, immediately append its matching closing symbol.
options.feedback: For p=2 this produces only "()()" and misses "(())".

options.text: Generate every length-2p binary choice string, then retain exactly those satisfying both totals and every prefix check.
options.feedback: This is correct, but explores prefixes already known to be invalid; prefix budget tests eliminate that removable work.

feedback.reason: The inequalities are necessary for every valid prefix and leave every valid continuation reachable. Both budgets must be exhausted before emitting.
details: Carry counts opened and closed. Append an opening symbol if opened<p, and a closing symbol if closed<opened. Undo each append. Copy the path when both counts equal p.

Never close more groups than have opened, and never open more than p. These prefix constraints prune invalid strings before completion. Undo each appended symbol so sibling branches start from the same valid prefix.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze `acm-b18-04-search` only. Let V count recursive calls of the revealed prefix method and R count all characters copied into returned strings. There is no preprocessing. Choose the tightest stated time and auxiliary-space pair. Count recursion and mutable working state; exclude supplied input and returned output storage, but include copying work in time. Primitive integer/index operations and preallocated-array updates cost constant time; dynamic appends are amortized constant time. No hashing is used unless explicitly stated.

options.text: O(V + R) time, O(p) auxiliary space
O(V + R) time, O(R) auxiliary space
O(p·V + R) time, O(p) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: At most two choices per state add search work plus emitted-string characters.
details: Each call has at most two constant-cost choices. Each emitted string is copied character by character, adding exactly R work.
A complete string reaches depth 2p. Path and stack are linear in p.
Let V count recursive calls of the revealed prefix method and R count all characters copied into returned strings. There is no preprocessing.
“O(V) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: This omits both output copying and the depth-2p stack.
“O(V + R) time, O(R) auxiliary space”: Returned strings are excluded and the method retains only one active prefix.
“O(p·V + R) time, O(p) auxiliary space”: Balances are updated incrementally rather than rescanned at every call.
